summary: Defines how Fibre Channel over TCP/IP (FCIP) entities can be found using the Service Location Protocol version 2 (SLPv2). It specifies the service information that FCIP devices advertise so peers can locate them without manual configuration.

eli5.summary: Instead of memorizing where each friend lives, you ask a bulletin board that lists who is nearby. This document says how storage gateways write their names on it.

questions: what is an fcip discovery domain
subtitle: How FCIP gateways advertise themselves and find each other using the Service Location Protocol, with two service templates.

tldr.problem: FCIP Entities need the IP address and port of their peers before they can connect, and configuring each one by hand does not scale.
tldr.mechanism: Each FCIP Entity registers a service:fcip:entity advertisement with SLPv2, with attributes such as its name and discovery domains, and looks up peers by querying on those attributes.
tldr.outcome: Peers can be found dynamically within administrator-defined discovery domains. RFC 3822 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 7146.

today: RFC 3822 is a Proposed Standard from July 2004 and is updated by RFC 7146. It has not been obsoleted. It works together with RFC 3821.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 3822 describes how the Service Location Protocol version 2 (SLPv2) is used to dynamically discover participating Fibre Channel over TCP/IP (FCIP) Entities, the gateways described in RFC 3821. It gives implementation guidelines, two service type templates and security considerations. It uses the RFC 2119 requirement words.

At least two FCIP Entities must be involved, and the end result is that an entity discovers one or more peers.
sections.eli5: Storage gateways need to find each other. This note explains how they can look each other up instead of someone typing in addresses.

sections.title: SLP and FCIP Terms
sections.content:
SLP has three kinds of agent. A User Agent (UA) works for a client and retrieves service information. A Service Agent (SA) advertises a service and its capabilities. A Directory Agent (DA) collects advertisements. A scope is a named set of services, typically one administrative group. An advertisement is a URL, attributes and a lifetime.

On the FCIP side, an FCIP Entity is the principal FCIP interface point to the IP network. Its name is the world wide name of the switch if it lives in a switch, otherwise the world wide node name of the associated Nx_Port. An FCIP Discovery Domain says which entities may discover each other within a scope.
sections.eli5: There are people who post notices (service agents), people who read notices (user agents) and a person who keeps the big notice board (the directory agent).

sections.title: How Discovery Works
sections.content:
Each FCIP Entity has a control and services module that talks to an SLPv2 SA and UA. The SA builds a service:fcip:entity advertisement for each service URL it wants to register, with a lifetime and the attributes defined in the template.

If a DA is found, the SA registers the advertisement with it. Whether or not a DA exists, the SA keeps the advertisement itself and answers multicast queries directly. When an entity needs a peer, its UA sends an SLPv2 service request, by unicast to the DA or by multicast to SAs, with a query describing the peers it wants. With the peer's IP address and port, it begins the normal connection procedure from RFC 3821. Using a DA is RECOMMENDED.

Discovery domains add control within a scope. In the RFC's example, scope fcip has domains purple, orange and blue. Purple lets entities A, B and C see each other, orange lets A see B but not C, and blue lets C see B but not A.
sections.eli5: You ask the bulletin board for gateways of a certain kind and get back their addresses. Clubs (discovery domains) decide who is allowed to see whom.

sections.title: The Two Service Templates
sections.content:
Two templates are defined. The abstract service:fcip is a top-level service that can hold future FCIP-related templates. The concrete service:fcip:entity is what a device registers for each FCIP Entity and each of its addresses.

The entity template has these attributes: fcip-entity-name (the Fibre Channel Switch Name for a switch-based entity, otherwise the Node Name of the associated port), transports (currently tcp only), an optional mgmt-entity list of management URLs, and fcip-discovery-domain naming the domains the entity belongs to. The URL carries a host and an optional port; a DNS host name should be used with the IANA well-known FCIP port for use with NAT and NAPT devices.

Typical queries find one entity by name, find all entities in a discovery domain, or, for a management application, list all entities with no query.
sections.eli5: A template is a form. Each gateway fills in its name, how it connects, how to manage it and which clubs it belongs to.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
The SLPv2 security model gives authentication so that UAs can trust advertisements from trusted SAs, but no confidentiality, and it cannot authenticate zero-result responses. After an entity is discovered, authentication and authorization are handled by the FCIP protocol itself.

Without SLP security there is a risk of false discovery information. When that matters, IPsec SAs SHOULD be used for FCIP traffic, so that an attacker advertising itself as an endpoint cannot finish IKE authentication. A remaining risk is denial of service by false information that triggers repeated IKE negotiation. Three countermeasures MUST be implemented: IP address range limits, DNS domain limits and a negative authentication cache.

IPsec SHOULD be implemented for SLPv2 as in RFC 3723, including ESP with a non-null transform. Because FCIP has its own authentication, SLPv2 authentication is OPTIONAL.
sections.eli5: Anyone could write a fake note on the board. So gateways prove who they are before they trust a stranger, and they stop talking to ones that fail.
